thread:
incident-bot: PAGED #incidents @oncall - decode-pool-3 reports repeated CUDA OOMs during streaming decode. Approx 12 nodes flapping, ~18% request drops, latency spike 4x. AlertID=INCD-6954321
maya: seeing the spike in the dashboard, lots of streaming failures with 'cuda runtime error: out of memory' in the decode path. customers: a few high-traffic tenants showing request drops.
oncall-alex: I'm awake, joining. pulling recent kube events + container logs.
rami: preliminary logs show the same pattern as previous runaway-gen incidents — requests with huge token budgets (max_tokens=200000+) bypassed client-side guard. kernel logs: `CUDA out of memory` on decode kernel. sample:```
[2026-03-17T02:45:21Z] decode_worker: alloc 512MB -> cudaMalloc failed: out of memory
[2026-03-17T02:45:21Z] decode_worker: user_request id=7a9b, max_tokens=200000, stream=true
[2026-03-17T02:45:21Z] gpu_monitor: eviction triggered, container restarts=3
```
eng_runtime_emma: confirmed. KV-cache growth + unbounded generation. Router forwarded a chunk of requests with `X-Client-Max-Tokens: 200000`. Our enforced cap at the proxy wasn't applied because of an internal header name mismatch after the last rollout.
sre_lead: status? cylce of node restarts will keep causing drops until we stop the inflight runaway streams. mitigation options: 1) route/deny requests with > maxtok cap at LB, 2) kill decode pods on the affected node (fast but noisy), 3) throttle streaming at router to 8 tokens/sec.
ops_jordan: I'm pushing a temporary firewall rule at the edge: `if X-Client-Max-Tokens > 2000 reject 413`. Applying to region-us-east now.
oncall-alex: doing a controlled eviction of the top 3 busiest pods on decode-pool-3 to free memory and break runaway streams. issuing: `kubectl -n inference delete pod <pod>` with readiness-probe off.
maya: thumbs up. notify customers impacted once we have scope.
eng_runtime_emma: patch to router is ready — hotfix will canonicalize header name and enforce `max_tokens <= 5000`. Pushing canary to 10% now. command:```bash
kubectl -n router rollout restart deploy/router-canary
# canary config: enforce-header: X-Client-Max-Tokens -> X-Redwood-Max-Tokens
```
rami: logs after canary show rejected requests with proper 413/ERR_PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE for the bad header. memory pressure decreasing on the canary-backed nodes.
sre_lead: ops_jordan, keep an eye on restart churn. If restarts > 5/min escalate to infra rotation.
ops_jordan: copy. I'm also pinning an emergency autoscale rule: max-pods=0 for decode-pool-3 to avoid bursty auto-provisioning while clearing backlog.
cust_success_liz: I'm drafting a short customer note for impacted tenants: one-liner + ETA. Suggest: "We observed transient request drops due to runaway generation from a client sending excessive max_tokens. We've deployed mitigations and the system is stabilizing. We'll follow up with root cause and affected request IDs." ok?
maya: looks good. add known affected customer IDs: tenant-acme, tenant-messengerx. include a tokenized list of sample request IDs.
oncall-alex: handing off to night crew in 45m. action items before handoff:
- confirm canary at 10% -> promote to 100% (eng_runtime_emma)
- clear remaining inflight streaming sessions on decode-pool-3 (oncall-alex + ops_jordan)
- run memory/pager check > monitor for 30m (sre_lead)
- send customer note (cust_success_liz)
- create postmortem stub with timeline (maya)
maya: I'll own the postmortem stub. tagging in tickets: INCD-6954321, PMT-3789.
eng_runtime_emma: canary promoted to 100%, enforcement is live across regions. seeing 90% reduction in OOM logs in the last 5m.
rami: telemetry shows request drops falling to baseline, GPU memory utilization back to normal.
sre_lead: good containment. leaving ops_jordan and oncall-alex on the bridge for handoff.
ops_jordan: leaving a short command summary for next oncall:
```
# emergency commands used during incident
kubectl -n inference delete pod <pod> --grace-period=0 --force  # evict runaway streams
kubectl -n router rollout restart deploy/router-canary  # push header-canonicalization hotfix
# temporary LB rule to block abusive requests by header
iptables -I INPUT -m string --algo bm --string "X-Client-Max-Tokens: 200000" -j DROP
```
oncall-alex: handoff to night oncall @team-night in 45m. please monitor the metrics channel for any recurrence.
cust_success_liz: customer notes sent for tenant-acme and tenant-messengerx. will follow up with churn risk checklist.
maya: postmortem stub created: https://pm.redwood.internal/INCD-6954321 - adding timeline + logs. closing channel in 2h unless new events. :white_check_mark:
